newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Ortega threatens more demonstrations in Nicaragua.
newsitem.headline: Ortega threatens more demonstrations in Nicaragua.

text.p: Nicaragua's Sandinista opposition, celebrating the anniversary of its 1979 revolution after weeks of mounting tension, threatened on Saturday to step up its demonstrations if the government did not bend to its demands.
The threat, by Sandinista leader Daniel Ortega, was made before thousands of demonstrators, who poured into the capital for the 17th anniversary of the most important day in the Sandinista calendar.

Facing a right-wing opposition government for the first time since its defeat in elections in November 1996, the Sandinista opposition is pressing the government for a more representative cabinet, to cut tariffs on public services, and to back student demands to devote six percent of the national budget to higher education.
Tensions have been high as the anniversary approached. Students have waged battles with police and clashes have left 150 wounded over the last three weeks.

"We are facing a government that disregards the law every day ... and he who commits crimes converts himself into a criminal and places himself outside the law," Ortega said. "The people are perfectly within their rights to seek justice."

Ortega proposed a referendum on government proposals to resolve the current crisis. "It is well worth having a referendum to ask whether we want a party that just does as it likes or if we want a national government," he said.
Sympathisers began arriving in Managua in the early hours of Saturday on foot, by car, bus and trucks. Houses bordering the square blared revolutionary music from their open doors.
